title: DecisionRanking
description: Why a StrategySet's candidates are in the order they are in, and which one is preferred. Until now the order was only the planner's output order and the core's blocking/restricted tiers, with no stored reason, so no eval could ask whether the ranking was supported (E9.1-E9.8). A DecisionRanking is written in the same transaction as its StrategySet from the tier inputs the core used and the reasons the worker's rank step gave. It judges nothing itself: the ranking evals read it. Immutable once written; choosing never changes it. abstained is true exactly when the preferred candidate is a quiet move (wait, no action, internal note) or the set has no acceptable candidate.

order.description: Candidate ids, best first: the order the candidates are shown in.

preferred_candidate_id.description: The first candidate in order. It is the ordering anchor, never a recommendation when the set has no acceptable candidate.

tier_inputs.description: What the core's tiering saw for each candidate, so the reasons can be checked against it (E9.8).

blocking.description: A blocking eval failed on this candidate.

restricted.description: The transition policy restricts this candidate's action class.

worker_rank.description: The rank the worker's planner gave before the core tiered.

pairwise_reasons.description: One reason for every adjacent pair in order, so the whole order is explained: n candidates give n - 1 reasons. A reason without evidence is a weaker reason, not an absent one.
